name: Grammarly
freeTierNote: $0 plan with spelling/grammar, tone, and 100 AI prompts/mo.
bestFor: Non-native and native writers who need a always-on editor in the browser
skipIf: You want long-form strategy or SEO briefs from a content platform
keyFeatures: Works inline across browsers, email, and docs
Reliable typo and clarity checks for non-native writers
limitations: Tone suggestions can flatten personal voice
Not built for long-form research or coding
summary: The grammar layer. Unsexy, widely installed, still the right first paid writing tool for many people.
body: Grammarly is not trying to be your novelist. It sits in the text box. For a developer writing English as a second language, that is worth more than Jasper’s campaign templates. Generative features now crowd the product; the core is still correctness. Annual Pro billing drops significantly below the $30 monthly rate.
notes: Turn off tone features if they flatten your voice
Enterprise DLP matters on corporate laptops
Claude is better for rewriting a whole chapter
